cards.back: Pay an invoice only when the purchase order (ordered), goods receipt (arrived) and invoice (billed) agree. No LLM output can approve a payment.
A workflow: the steps are known, so a fixed Postgres state machine runs them. The agent is a bounded loop that runs inside one state, only for exceptions.
One transaction moves the case row, writes an append-only audit event and queues the next job, so a crash never loses or doubles a step.
Fetch, render to PNG within 1664 × 2048, parse each page with Nemotron Parse, then an LLM extracts a Document at temperature 0, validated by Pydantic with one retry.
Every amount in the PDF's own text layer must appear in the parsed text. It caught the $1,374.60 total the parser dropped on invoice 11077.
Plain code: lines joined by normalised product name, prices compared with a 0.01 tolerance, nine exception codes, and any exception means no approval.
Runs only in INVESTIGATING, with at most 8 read-only tool calls and a fixed token budget. Hitting a limit hands the case to a person.
Memory is written only when a person closes a case, so a malicious invoice cannot teach a bad precedent.
pgmq in the same Postgres, batches of 10 with a 60 s visibility timeout, backoff of 2^n × 10 s, and a dead-letter queue after 5 attempts.

cards.front: Approval bound to an action hash
cards.back: The approval stores a hash of the action. The executor recomputes it, re-reads the PO and invoice, and writes with idempotency key case_id:action before reading it back.
Zero bad invoices reaching approval as clean, 100% exact duplicates caught, zero unsafe actions on the injection suite, 98% field accuracy, 85% agent root cause.

quiz.q: A queue job is delivered twice after a worker crash. Why does the second delivery do nothing?
choices: pgmq guarantees exactly-once delivery
The handler locks the case row and runs the step only if the case is still in the state the job was queued for
The LLM notices it already ran
Cloud Run deduplicates requests
quiz.why: Each job names its state, so a repeat delivery finds the case already moved and does nothing.

quiz.q: An invoice's extracted total is empty, though the PDF clearly shows one. What most likely happened and what does the design do?
choices: The parser dropped the value; the text-layer cross-check reports it and extraction leaves the total empty rather than guessing
The LLM was told to round totals
The matcher deleted it as a duplicate
The PDF was quarantined for injection
quiz.why: On invoice 11077 the parser dropped $1,374.60 and the cross-check caught it; the prompt forbids guessing values.

quiz.q: Between approval and execution, the vendor edits the invoice amount. What stops the old approval from paying the new amount?
choices: The approver's amount limit
The resolution agent rechecks it
Nothing; approvals are final
The executor recomputes the action hash and re-reads the PO and invoice, stopping if either changed
quiz.why: Approval is bound to an action hash, and the executor stops on any change.

quiz.q: A PDF contains hidden text telling the agent to approve the invoice. Where should the case go?
choices: To the resolution agent with a warning
Straight to AWAITING_APPROVAL
QUARANTINED, to a person and never the agent
BLOCKED_DUPLICATE
quiz.why: An injection or tampering signal at SCREENING moves the case to QUARANTINED for a person.

quiz.q: The agent proposes a corrected unit price and asks rerun_match to approve the case. When is that correction accepted?
choices: When the agent's confidence is above 0.9
Only when the correction comes from a second source
Always, since the agent has read-only tools
Only after 8 tool calls
quiz.why: rerun_match accepts only corrections from a second source, so the agent cannot talk the matcher into a pass.

quiz.q: One job keeps failing. After how many attempts does it leave the main queue, and where does it go?
choices: After 3, back to RECEIVED
After 10, it is deleted
Never; it retries forever with backoff
After 5, to jobs_dlq
quiz.why: A failed job reappears after 2^n × 10 s and moves to the dead-letter queue after 5 attempts.

quiz.q: Why does the queue live in the same Postgres as the cases instead of a separate broker?
choices: So a state change and its next job commit together in one transaction
Because brokers cannot do retries
To let the LLM read the queue
Because pgvector requires it
quiz.why: With pgmq in the same database, the state move and the next job commit together.
